content.title: About
content.content: Canned pineapple in syrup consists of bite‑size pieces of ripe pineapple that have been heat‑treated and sealed in a sweet sugar syrup. The product retains the characteristic aroma and sweetness of fresh pineapple while offering a long shelf life.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pineapple is one of the few tropical fruits that is widely canned on an industrial scale.
The syrup is usually made from sugar and water, sometimes with a touch of citric acid to preserve the bright color.
Canned pineapple is a common ingredient in desserts, salads, and cocktails.
In the 19th century, canning pineapple became a popular way to ship this exotic fruit to markets without fresh supplies.
Pineapple in syrup can contain up to 20 % added sugar, making it more caloric than fresh fruit.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Pineapple provides a good amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains bromelain
items.content: The enzyme bromelain aids protein digestion and has anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Source of manganese
items.content: Manganese is involved in carbohydrate metabolism and bone formation.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Potassium in pineapple helps maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The syrup adds a significant amount of sugar, which may be problematic for people with diabetes or those watching their weight.

items.title: Pineapple allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pineapple, ranging from skin rashes to swelling.

items.title: Presence of preservatives
items.content: Certain brands add preservatives such as potassium sorbate; those with sensitivities should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned pineapple can be enjoyed straight from the jar, added to fruit salads, yogurts, baked goods, smoothies, and ice cream. The syrup is often drained, but a small amount can be used as a sweetener.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the fruit refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if mold appears or an off‑odor develops.
